name: Larry Kelly

bio.statement: Kelly's voters' pamphlet statement lists 20 years in the restaurant industry.
Kelly's pamphlet statement lists a BS in biochemistry from Western Washington University.
Kelly's city filing form lists his occupation as chef at Jam on Hawthorne.

bio.statement: The Portland Mercury reports Kelly moved to Portland from Bellingham, Washington, two years ago.

positions.statement: In his voters' pamphlet statement, Kelly says people who work in Portland should be able to afford to live there.

positions.statement: Kelly's pamphlet statement says homelessness must be met with compassion and dignity while being honest about what is working.
positions.excerpt: We must confront homelessness with compassion and dignity while being honest about what is and isn’t working.

positions.statement: Kelly's pamphlet statement says Portland needs to expand mental health and addiction services.
positions.excerpt: Portland needs to expand its mental health and addiction services.

positions.statement: OPB reports Kelly wants the city to improve its relationship with small businesses.
positions.excerpt: Larry Kelly is a chef who wants to see the city improve its relationship with small businesses.

positions.statement: Kelly's pamphlet statement calls for evidence-based decisions, measuring results and transparency with the community.
positions.excerpt: making evidence-based decisions, measuring results, and being transparent with the community.

collection_notes: Steps run identically for all 21 District 3 candidates: (1) county Military & Overseas Online Voters' Guide statement PDF (with the full and large-print county pamphlets tried where the statement PDF was a scan; the pamphlet's candidate index marks candidates who filed no statement) plus the City Auditor's AUD-120 candidate filing form linked from portland.gov's 2026 city candidates page; (2) portland.gov/council roster and councilor page for incumbents; (3) campaign domain only as printed in the pamphlet statement or filing form; (4) one general WebSearch; (5) three fixed allowed-domain WebSearch groups (opb.org+oregoncapitalchronicle.com+wweek.com+ballotpedia.org; kgw.com+koin.com+kptv.com+katu.com; portlandmercury.com+vote411.org+pamplinmedia.com+portlandtribune.com) because the search proxy rejects oregonlive.com and apnews.com; (6) the three articles that cover the whole District 3 field: OPB 'What to know about Portland's District 3 council race' (2026-10-07), Portland Mercury 'Meet the Candidates For City Council District 3' (2026-09-09) and Portland Tribune 'Meet the Portland City Council District 3 candidates' (2026-10-13; Q&A — the Tribune says Sollitt, Pham, Parker, McCormick, Kelly and Frankenstein did not respond and Tucker withdrew). Multi-winner race: OPB states three council seats are available in District 3. Excerpts come through a summarizing fetch tool that limits verbatim quotes to ~125 characters, so some are fragments. Ballot name/order match inventory.json and the county Ballot Content RCV report.
